notes.hierarchy: Each screen has a clear lead headline and CTA, though the services section's empty left column weakens the reading flow.
notes.typography: The bold tight headlines and spaced eyebrows give a consistent scale, but the system sans feels generic and one eyebrow size is inconsistent.
notes.color: The restrained indigo accent on soft lavender and dark navy is coherent and readable.
notes.layout: Compositions vary sensibly, but the services column imbalance and the repeated contact hero photo detract.
notes.spacing: Rhythm is mostly consistent, with some uneven gaps between sections and inside the contact cards.
notes.imagery: The photos are relevant and high quality, but the hero image is duplicated across pages and the mobile card crops sit unevenly.
notes.mobile: The phone layout is deliberately stacked and centered, with readable text and usable controls.
notes.consistency: Both pages share the same components, footer, colours and type.
notes.polish: The site is clean overall, with a few rough details in the contact cards and image fitting.
notes.fit: The tone suits a general clinic and the navigation to contact and visit information is clear, without overclaiming details.

strengths: Clear hero with a strong headline, a short supporting line, and a primary pill CTA paired with a secondary text link.
Coherent indigo/lavender palette with dark navy surfaces gives the site a calm clinic tone and good contrast.
Section surfaces alternate (lavender, white, off-white, indigo CTA band, dark footer), echoing the source layout's rhythm.
Placeholders are honest, with no fabricated phone, hours or address, and emergency guidance is handled responsibly.
Mobile is recomposed with centered hero text, a Menu button, stacked cards and comfortable tap targets.
Photography is warm, relevant and consistently treated with rounded corners.
issues: Services section on desktop leaves a large empty lavender column under the sticky-less intro text, creating an unbalanced left half for most of the section's height.
Contact hero reuses nearly the same photo as the home hero, so the two pages feel repetitive and the contact page gains no new visual information.
Contact 'Where to find us' card has an odd internal hierarchy: an oversized 'Sample City' sits above a divider that hugs it too tightly, and 'Opening hours' is cramped against that rule.
'How to get in touch' card eyebrow is set larger and with different tracking than the other eyebrows, and its top padding is inconsistent with the adjacent card.
Typography is a system sans (Arial/Helvetica-like) throughout, so the type is readable but generic, not distinctive.
Mobile service card images don't span the full card width; they leave an uneven right gap inside the card.
The large empty gap between the contact cards and the 'What to ask us about' section is bigger than the other section gaps.

notes.hierarchy: The main message and section priorities are clear, though a few mid-page CTAs and informational blocks compete rather than creating a single next step.
notes.typography: The type scale, weight contrast and line spacing are consistent and readable, with only a slightly generic sans-serif feel keeping it from exceptional.
notes.color: The lavender, purple, white and dark footer palette is coherent and accessible-looking, with the accent generally controlled.
notes.layout: The compositions are balanced overall, but the desktop service area and some list sections feel a bit repetitive or underfilled.
notes.spacing: Margins, gutters and card padding are mostly precise, with only a few areas where wide separation weakens grouping.
notes.imagery: The photos are high quality and relevant, but they read as generic stock and are reused enough to reduce distinctiveness.
notes.mobile: The phone views are comfortable and intentionally stacked with usable buttons and readable copy.
notes.consistency: Both pages and breakpoints use a very coherent component, color, type and spacing system.
notes.polish: Buttons, rounded cards, borders, footer and section transitions are clean, though not every section feels fully bespoke.
notes.fit: The tone suits a general-care clinic and the placeholder contact information is handled responsibly, but the main visitor action could be more prominent.

strengths: The hero areas have a clear focal point, strong headline, useful introductory copy and obvious next actions.
Typography is highly readable, with confident large headings, clear labels and comfortable body text across desktop and mobile.
The palette is calm, medical-appropriate and coherent, with purple used consistently for emphasis and navigation.
Mobile layouts are deliberately recomposed with readable text, large controls, stacked cards and well-contained imagery.
The site respects the brief by using graceful placeholders for unknown address, hours and phone details rather than inventing specifics.
The Home and Contact pages share a cohesive visual system, including the same header, buttons, rounded imagery, section labels and footer treatment.
issues: The services section on desktop leaves a very large inactive left column while the right-side cards stack, making that area feel a little empty after the intro copy.
Imagery is polished but feels somewhat generic and repetitive, with the same consultation photo reused across both hero pages and similar clinical stock-style thumbnails throughout.
Some calls to action are secondary or indirect for a clinic visitor: there is no single dominant contact/booking pathway, and several links point to informational sections instead.
The desktop emergency/contact strip on the Contact page separates the heading and explanatory text widely, which weakens the grouping of related information.
The design is clean but relies heavily on repeated rounded cards, pale lavender panels and text-link rows, so a few middle sections feel template-like rather than highly bespoke.

notes.hierarchy: The visual hierarchy is generally strong and guides the eye logically, though tight spacing in the mobile footer slightly blurs the grouping of links.
notes.typography: The typography is distinctive, highly readable, and maintains a consistent, deliberate scale across all breakpoints.
notes.color: The palette is confident, coherent, and perfectly suited to a medical clinic, providing excellent contrast and a calming tone.
notes.layout: Layouts are varied and balanced, successfully adapting the source inspiration, though the side-by-side cards on the Contact page lack equal height.
notes.spacing: Spacing is mostly consistent and establishes a good rhythm, but minor padding imbalances in lists and tight mobile footer gaps detract slightly.
notes.imagery: The selected images are high-quality, relevant to the clinic's services, and beautifully integrated into the rounded-corner layout.
notes.mobile: The mobile layout is thoughtfully composed and comfortable to use, with only minor spacing refinements needed in the footer.
notes.consistency: The visual language, including components, colors, and typography, is exceptionally coherent across both pages and all screen sizes.
notes.polish: The design is very clean and professional overall, though a few minor details like card heights and list padding could be refined.
notes.fit: The design perfectly captures the required professional and reassuring tone, and handles the requested placeholders gracefully.

strengths: The color palette is cohesive, calming, and highly appropriate for a healthcare setting, providing excellent contrast for readability.
The typography system is well-defined, using scale and weight effectively to establish a clear visual hierarchy across all screen sizes.
The adaptation to mobile is deliberate and well-executed, ensuring that complex desktop layouts stack logically and remain easy to interact with.
The builder successfully implemented graceful placeholders for missing information (like hours and phone number) without breaking the design or sounding unprofessional.
issues: On the desktop Contact page, the 'Where to find us' and 'How to get in touch' cards are placed side-by-side but have unequal heights, disrupting the horizontal balance.
In the 'Three visits you can ask about' list on the Contact page, the vertical padding within each row appears slightly unbalanced, with more space below the link than above the title.
In the mobile footer, the vertical spacing between the section headings (e.g., 'PAGES') and their corresponding links is very tight, making the groupings feel slightly cramped.

notes.hierarchy: Each screen has a clear lead headline and CTA, though the contact grid flattens emphasis.
notes.typography: The scale and spacing are comfortable, but the serif headings look like a default fallback.
notes.color: The soft, coherent palette has a restrained purple accent and good contrast.
notes.layout: Sections vary sensibly (split hero, cards, numbered list, CTA band), though some areas are template-like and sparse.
notes.spacing: Generally aligned to a consistent container, with a few oversized empty gaps and uneven card widths.
notes.imagery: The original flat illustration is pleasant, but the clinician icon tile feels placeholder-ish.
notes.mobile: The phone layout is composed for the small screen, with stacked CTAs, readable type and an accessible menu button.
notes.consistency: Both pages share the header, footer, card styles and palette coherently.
notes.polish: Clean overall, with rough spots in the card-width mismatch, the avatar caption and the footer links.
notes.fit: The tone suits a general clinic, and the contact actions are obvious and honestly framed.

strengths: Calm lavender/cream/sage/peach palette suits a clinic and uses the purple accent with restraint.
The hero has a clear headline, supporting copy and a primary/secondary CTA pair, plus a tasteful original illustration.
Unknown details are handled honestly with graceful placeholders and no fabricated data or fake form.
Alternating surface colours give the page a clear rhythm, consistent with the reference structure.
The mobile layout is properly reflowed, with a labelled Menu button, full-width buttons and comfortable text size.
The emergency guidance is useful and consistent across pages.
issues: The serif display face looks like a system Times-style fallback, so headings feel default next to the more refined sans body text.
The first service card (lavender fill) differs from the other two (white) with no clear reason, and the three cards are visibly different widths in slice 2.
The clinician 'portrait' is a small stethoscope icon tile with a caption that is slightly offset and cramped under the circle; it reads as a placeholder.
There is a large empty band above the CTA and near the disclaimer (home slice 4, contact slice 3), which breaks the section rhythm.
On the contact page, six near-identical 'To be confirmed' cards dominate and the grid feels repetitive.
The footer link underlines and the bottom-border rule, which extends past the content width, look slightly unrefined.

notes.hierarchy: The main message and next actions are clear on both pages, though repeated card blocks reduce emphasis in some lower sections.
notes.typography: The serif headings and sans body create a readable, consistent system with comfortable line lengths, though not quite exceptional.
notes.color: The muted medical palette is cohesive, calm and readable, with the purple accent used effectively for actions and emphasis.
notes.layout: Sections are generally varied and balanced, but the card grids and stacked mobile contact details feel somewhat repetitive.
notes.spacing: Alignment is strong and spacing is mostly deliberate, with only a few transitions feeling more spacious than necessary.
notes.imagery: The custom-looking clinic illustration and icons fit the subject, but they remain fairly simple and slightly generic.
notes.mobile: The phone layout is comfortable and readable, although the contact page relies on a long sequence of large stacked cards.
notes.consistency: Home and Contact clearly belong to the same system across desktop and mobile.
notes.polish: Most details are finished and calm, but the footer link styling and generic graphic treatment keep it short of studio-perfect.
notes.fit: The design suits a fictional general-care clinic very well and makes the available actions and unavailable details clear without fabricating information.

strengths: The site has a calm, polished healthcare tone with a coherent lavender, cream and deep-purple palette.
The brief is handled carefully: unknown contact, booking, hours, address and reviews are clearly marked as unavailable rather than invented.
The desktop layouts are balanced, with a strong hero, clear calls to action, useful service copy and well-structured clinician and preparation sections.
Mobile typography and controls are readable, with large tap targets and a clear simplified header.
The two pages share a consistent visual system, including type, cards, rounded corners, colours, disclaimers and footer treatment.
issues: Several mid-page sections use similar rounded-card patterns, so parts of the services and contact-detail areas feel slightly template-like rather than fully bespoke.
The mobile contact page becomes a long stack of large cards with repeated placeholder text, which is clear but not very efficient for scanning.
Some footer links appear as plain underlined text, which is accessible but less refined than the rest of the component styling.
The illustrations and icons are clean and relevant, but they have a simple placeholder quality rather than feeling like a fully distinctive clinic image system.
There are a few very generous vertical gaps between sections, especially around transitions into large content blocks, which slightly slows the reading rhythm.

notes.hierarchy: The use of scale, color, and layout creates an unmistakable reading order and clear focal points on every screen.
notes.typography: The pairing of a refined serif for headings with a clean sans-serif for body text is highly readable and sets a premium tone.
notes.color: The soft purple and beige palette is calming and appropriate, with darker tones providing excellent contrast for text and interactive elements.
notes.layout: Sections are varied and well-balanced, using columns and cards effectively to organize complex information without feeling cluttered.
notes.spacing: There is a rigorous and consistent spacing system that gives the content room to breathe and establishes a clear rhythm.
notes.imagery: The custom vector illustrations are high-quality, fit the clinic's approachable tone, and are perfectly integrated into the layouts.
notes.mobile: While the visible mobile components are beautifully adapted, the apparent omission of key sections in the homepage flow slightly impacts the overall experience.
notes.consistency: The visual language is flawlessly maintained across all pages, components, and screen sizes.
notes.polish: The design is extremely refined overall, though minor details like text-based arrows and default link underlines offer slight room for improvement.
notes.fit: The design perfectly captures the required tone and handles the brief's constraints regarding missing information with elegance and clarity.

strengths: The color palette and typography establish a highly professional, calming, and trustworthy tone perfectly suited for a medical practice.
The requirement for 'graceful placeholders' is executed brilliantly, using styled cards that clearly communicate missing information without looking like errors.
Custom illustrations and a rigorous spacing system create a cohesive, premium visual language across all viewports.
issues: The mobile homepage screenshots omit the 'Preparing for a visit' and main CTA sections, creating an abrupt jump in the user journey.
The 'Full visit preparation ->' link uses a basic text arrow (hyphen and greater-than sign) rather than a polished vector icon.
Footer navigation links rely on default browser underlines that sit tight against the text, missing a final touch of typographic refinement.

note: Each site is scored on its own (absolute), from screenshots, with tool names hidden. Radial Pulse generates with an Anthropic model, so scores are also reported without the Anthropic judge.
